item.title: The US Economy Needs Silicon Valley, Wall Street and Hollywood
item.description: Even more so than usual, Hollywood’s future is uncertain. For decades the Los Angeles economy revolved around the film industry, but now more movies and shows are filmed elsewhere, driven or lured away by high expenses or tax incentives. The prospect of Paramount leaving California over the state’s antitrust lawsuit may not be serious, but the very idea that it can be entertained shows how much the economics of the industry have changed.
item.dc:creator: Allison Schrager

item.title: Colorado River Cuts Will Force Southwest to Choose Between Cows and People
item.description: Sustaining communities of millions of thirsty people in a desert is challenging enough. Adding millions more cows, or at least growing the water-intensive food those cows eat, ramps up the difficulty level exponentially. America’s arid Southwest is learning it can’t comfortably have both.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gongloff

item.title: For the New CDC Director, Damage Control Would Be a Big Win
item.description: Through little fault of her own, the nation’s new head of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention starts her job with low expectations. It’s not just her boss’s antipathy for the agency, which he has called a “cesspool of corruption.” Within days of Erica Schwartz’s confirmation as director, the president issued an executive order seeking to overhaul the childhood vaccine schedule — with no new supporting evidence.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Measles Outbreak Exposes Florida Republicans’ Vaccine Problem
item.description: Republicans have painted themselves into a corner by undermining vaccines. Nowhere is this clearer than Florida, where the outgoing Republican governor and his potential successor have tried to use vaccine mandates to align themselves with President Donald Trump’s politically risky position.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: Big Tech Cannot Be Trusted to Regulate Its AI Creations
item.description: Bill Gates, the billionaire co-founder of Microsoft Corp., published a 6,000-word essay on Aug. 26 saying that he would slow the development of artificial intelligence if he could. item.title: Trump Is Copying Putin’s Losing Playbook With Canada
item.description: It sometimes feels as though the Trump administration gets its worldview and foreign policy ideas from a Kremlin School of International Relations course taught by Vladimir Putin — though at a CliffsNotes level that fails to consider how those strategies played out.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: Tanzania Dam Is a Massive Moment for African Self-Finance
item.description: Four years ago, Tanzania was so short of power that its state-run utility said electricity would be rationed, with some areas cut off for nine hours a day. But by last week, when President Samia Suluhu Hassan officially opened a giant new hydropower plant on the country’s largest river, the Rufiji, it had become a power-surplus nation.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Sharma

item.title: Welcome to the Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell AI Economy
item.description: Do you have any artificial intelligence secrets? Maybe the better question: Would it concern you if your most intimate chatbot queries were shared with your family, colleagues or bosses?
item.dc:creator: Catherine Thorbecke

item.title: Children Should Be More Than a Luxury
item.description: It's increasingly apparent that humanity won’t be returning to levels of fertility that helped quadruple the world’s population over the past century. Wistful state programs almost guarantee disappointment, given households are getting smaller — and costlier. But some political leaders aren’t giving up yet.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss
